SettingTips.BuffWait:
Seconds added after buffs (Veneration, Innovation, Great Strides, Waste Not, Manipulation), which wait 2 s by default; the previous setting applies to the other actions (3 s by default). Until changed, it equals the actions’ one.
Default: 0.
SettingTips.OpenOnLastPage:
Unticked: Tensho opens on Home when the plugin loads; during a session, the reopened window keeps its page. Ticked: the last page shown comes back, even after reloading Tensho or restarting the game (it is saved when the window or the plugin closes). The Diagnostics page only comes back in developer mode.
Default: off (Home).
SettingTips.ViewConeColor: View cone colour; its opacity is the setting just above. Default: the theme's gold.
SettingTips.PlayerIconScale: Size of the arrow showing your position on the Tensho map. Default: 100%.
SettingTips.ViewConeScale: Length of the view cone in front of your position. Default: 100%.
SettingTips.ViewConeOpacity: View cone opacity: 0% = invisible, 100% = solid. Default: 50%.
SettingTips.Language: Tensho language. Default: the game's. Missing texts of a language are shown in English.
SettingTips.Theme: Tensho colours. « Follow the game » uses the theme chosen in the game options. Default: follow the game.
SettingTips.CraftLog: Macro help panel beside the game's crafting log, for the open recipe.
SettingTips.Steps: Maximum number of actions explored by the crafting rotation search. Higher = longer to compute.
SettingTips.Width: Number of paths kept at each step of the search. Higher = better possible result, but slower.
SettingTips.Budget: Maximum number of transitions examined before the search stops. Avoids very long computations on big recipes.
SettingTips.Wait: Seconds added after each action in generated macros (network lag). 0 = the game's normal waits.
SettingTips.Echo: Adds a sound message line at the end of each generated macro block, to know it has finished.
SettingTips.MacroBook: Where macros are copied in the game: individual (this character) or shared (all characters).
SettingTips.MacroStart: First game macro slot used by the copy (0 to 99).
SettingTips.MacroEnd: Last slot the copy may use; beyond it, the copy stops.
SettingTips.MacroPrefix: Name of the copied macros, followed by the page (for example « Tensho 1/3 »). Overwriting unticked: only macros named exactly this way are replaced; empty name: only empty slots are used. 12 characters at most.
SettingTips.MacroOverwrite: Ticked: the copy may replace any macro in the chosen slots. Unticked: only empty slots or slots Tensho copied before.
SettingTips.MacroChain: Ends each page with /tenshonext so Tensho's Macro chain starts the next page (long rotations).
SettingTips.PlaceNameScale: Size of place names on the Tensho map. Default: 100%.
SettingTips.IconScale: Size of all map icons, on top of each icon's own size. Default: 100%.
SettingTips.Opacity: Transparency of the map window. Default: 100% (opaque).
SettingTips.AlarmGroupOn: Turns all the alarms of this item on or off at once.
SettingTips.AlarmOn: Turns this alarm on or off.
SettingTips.AlarmLead: Minutes of warning before the window starts (real time). Bounded by the alarm's repetition.
SettingTips.CachePrices: How long a price read from Universalis is reused without a new request. « Never » = on request only.
SettingTips.CacheQuests: Interval between reads of the quest list in the game. « Never » = only with « Refresh ».
SettingTips.CacheCollections: How long read collections (mounts, minions, cards…) are kept before reading again.
SettingTips.CacheCompletion: How long the state of titles and achievements stays known after a read.
SettingTips.CacheSources: How long community sources are kept (Garland, wiki, LuminaSupplemental, GatherBuddy, Teamcraft).
SettingTips.CacheFashion: How long Fashion Report data are kept.
SettingTips.CacheImportedStock: After this time, retainer and saddlebag stocks are flagged as old (they stay shown).
SettingTips.CacheCraftCalculations: How long crafting calculations (simulations, rotations) are kept.
SettingTips.AreaColour: Colour and transparency of these areas on the map (click to choose it).
SettingTips.ItemSearchLimit:
How many items the search lists at most: Items page, and the item picker of Monster loot and NPC vendors. Higher = a longer list to scroll; beyond it, refine your search (10 to 100).
Default: 30.
SettingTips.GameFrames:
Draws the game's window frame behind Tensho's main window (textures read from the game files). If a texture is missing, for example after a game update, the window keeps its normal look.
Default: off.

Settings.HoverCompareTip: Under a gear piece's tooltip: item level and stat difference with the piece worn in the same slot (both rings for a ring). Base values, no materia.
Settings.ResetAllTip:
Restores every Tensho setting (windows, map with its per-map icon sizes and priorities, tooltips, community sources, caches, theme, crafting search limits…) to its default value.
Kept: the language, the folded navigation groups, alarms, craft presets, Triple Triad decks, followed quests, map bookmarks, macro plan, sort profiles and templates, observations, reminders marked done, read vessels, unlocked sectors, the gear, materia and build plans, and the Discord webhook address (sending is turned off; « Clear » button of the Discord section to remove it). The bank is not touched. If saving fails, the previous values come back.
Settings.ResetAllConfirm: Restore every setting to its default? Your data (alarms, presets, decks…) is kept.

Settings.OpenOnLogin: Open when the character logs in

Settings.UsageHover: Show item uses when hovering items in game

Advanced.CloseOnGameWindow: Close Tensho when it opens a game window
Advanced.CloseOnGameWindowTip:
After « Open in the crafting log », « … gathering log » or « Game map », the Tensho window closes to show the game’s. A game window already open is opened on the entry, not closed.
Default: on.
Advanced.AlarmBarTooltipTip:
Hovering the alarm icon of the server bar shows Tensho's own tooltip just below it, above every window (the game's goes under plugin windows such as the Tensho map). Unticked: the game's tooltip.
Default: on.
Advanced.AlarmBarTooltipCountTip:
Number of upcoming alarms shown in the tooltip (1 to 10).
Default: 5.
Advanced.AlarmServerBar: Alarm icon in the server bar
Advanced.AlarmServerBarTip:
Shows a clock and the number of active Tensho alarms in the game's info bar (next to the server name); hover = next alarm; click = Alarms page. Hidden without an active alarm.
Default: on.
Advanced.ReminderServerBar: Reminders icon in the server bar
Advanced.ReminderServerBarTip:
Shows its own icon and the number of things left to do in the game's info bar: reminders not ticked since their reset and your tasks marked on screen; hover = the list; click = Reminders page. The Reminders page chooses what it shows (« Bar » boxes).
Default: on.
Advanced.ReminderFinishedServerBar: Finished reminders icon in the server bar
Advanced.ReminderFinishedServerBarTip:
Shows its own icon and the number of finished things (ventures, vessels back, squadron, ripe beds) in the game's info bar, only when there are some; hover = the list; click = Reminders page.
Default: on.
Advanced.TeamcraftTip: Time between the cast and the bite, per fish and spot, from Teamcraft's public reports (gubal API, MIT licence). One request per fishing spot, cached.
Advanced.GatherBuddyTip: GatherBuddy fishing data files (Ottermandias, Apache-2.0 licence): baits, mooches, bite and hookset, windows, weather, lures and predators. Downloaded once, cached.
Advanced.MarketMoved: Market prices on hover: Settings › Advanced › Community sources.
Advanced.Help: Settings to go further: restore all defaults, developer mode, community sources, game alarms and reporting help. Hover each setting for its explanation.
Advanced.HeaderClockTip: Shows the computer time next to the version, at the top of the window. It is the only place it appears.
Advanced.HeaderEtTip: Shows ET (1 ET day = 70 real minutes) next to the version. Gathering and weather tools show it too.
Advanced.HomeTools: Tool directory on the home page
Advanced.HomeToolsTip: Shows, at the bottom of the home page, the collapsible list of every tool with a short description, an Open button and its details.
Advanced.DeveloperTip: Adds the Diagnostics page (catalogue states, contributor help, probes), the Debug tab (translation keys) and game ids in tooltips. Saved.
Advanced.ShowIdsTip: Shows item ids (and other game rows) even without developer mode: useful to report a problem or search with the probes.
Advanced.SourcesHelp: Game data always comes first. Turning a source off stops its downloads; its lines disappear from tooltips.
Advanced.LuminaTip: Critical-Impact CSV files (GPL-3.0): duty coffers, monster drops, Eureka, desynthesis, card packs, NPCs of unlinked shops. Downloaded once, cached.
Advanced.GarlandTip: Item sources (duties, exchanges, NPCs) requested one at a time when the item is shown; community data, absent = unknown.
Advanced.WikiTip: Wiki acquisition pages (achievements, notes, vistas): English text, used when the game data says nothing.
Advanced.MarketTip: Universalis prices of the current world when hovering an item (network).
Advanced.CommandDelayTip: Wait between two alarms sent to the game. Raise it if the game ignores some when many are sent at once.
Advanced.ClearAlarmsTip: Empties the Tensho alarm list (not the game's). Two clicks to avoid mistakes.
Advanced.CopyReportTip: Copies the version, language, catalogue and source states, errors and alarm counts, without character data, to paste in a GitHub issue.
Advanced.CopyRepositoryTip: github.com/Shigu330/Tensho-Assistant: source code (GPL v3), issues, contributions.
Advanced.DutyFinderTip: Opens the loot panel next to the game's duty finder window.
Advanced.CharacterPanelTip: Opens the real stats panel (%) next to the game's Character window.
Advanced.ReloadTip: Reads the language files again without restarting the plugin.
Advanced.ObservationTip: Reads a game window live (nothing is changed); turn it off if you do not use the tool.
Advanced.LeadTip: Minutes before the slot when the alarm rings, for new alarms (each alarm keeps its own, editable).
Advanced.PlaySoundTip: Plays the game's alarm sound when a Tensho alarm rings.
Advanced.SoundTip: Game alarm sound (Bell, Music box…), also used for alarms sent to the game.
Advanced.ChatTip: Writes the alarm in the game chat (only you see it).
Advanced.MuteTip:
No sound while in a duty; the chat message stays, unless the option just below is ticked.
Default: on.
Advanced.MuteChatTip:
While you are in a duty, the alarm's [Tensho] line is not written in the chat either. No effect while « No sound in duties » or « Chat message » is unticked. Alarms copied into the game and Discord messages do not change.
Default: off.
Advanced.GameWeatherTip: The game rings every ET day without looking at the weather: tick only if that suits you.
Advanced.FashionTip:
Downloads the week's pieces and dyes from FFXIVGachaSpreadsheet (GitHub). Off: no download any more; a recent copy kept on disk is still shown.
Default: on.
Advanced.UniversalisTip:
Market prices and listings (Market page, hover prices, preparation cost, data centres), read from universalis.app. Off: no request to Universalis any more; prices already kept are still shown on the Market page, hover prices are hidden.
Default: on.
Advanced.SourceOffTip: Source turned off (Settings › Advanced › Community sources): no request is sent; a copy already kept is still shown where this page has one.
Advanced.HoverRefreshTip:
While hovering an item, Ctrl+Alt asks Universalis for its price again, even if recent (one request per press, at least 5 seconds apart).
Default: on.
Advanced.UndercutTip:
When you open an item's offers on the market board, Tensho copies the lowest offer minus 1 gil (your retainers left out) to the clipboard and says so in the chat. You paste and confirm in the game yourself: nothing is listed for you. Replaces the clipboard content.
Default: off.

GatheringPanel.NodeBonus: Major bonus on this node: GP is spent here.
GatheringPanel.SaveForBonus: Keep GP for nodes with a major bonus
GatheringPanel.SaveForBonusTip: A normal node spends only the GP that would be lost at the maximum. A node with more attempts, a higher quantity or a much higher extra chance than the plainest seen for this item spends it all. The first node seen counts as normal. Unticked: GP is shared evenly across the nodes.

GatheringPanel.ListNeedTooMany: Crafting list: {0} missing, out of reach in {1} nodes.

GatheringPanel.NodeSecondsTip: Your estimate. It sets how much GP comes back between nodes. From 5 to 600.
GatheringPanel.RegenTip: The GP that comes back every 3 seconds, for every job. 0 uses the value measured in game, with the traits each job has unlocked.

GatheringPanel.Footer: Click an item = context item; plan computed like the GP tool (estimated Bountiful).
GatheringPanel.SettingTip: Shows, beside the game's gathering window, the node's items (success, boon, stock, estimated Bountiful) and the advised GP plan, per job (miner / botanist). Turns on reading the gathering window (nothing is changed in the game); turning off « Observe the MIN/BTN node open in game » turns this help off too.
GatheringPanel.Missing: Plan not computed, value not read: {0} (no value is guessed).
GatheringPanel.AfterStart: Plan not computed: this item was first read after GP was spent at this node, so its rates may already include the bonuses bought.
GatheringPanel.PlanAtStart: Plan made when the node opened ({0} GP): the actions already used are part of it.
GatheringPanel.BountifulFloor: Bountiful bonus unknown (gathering rating or item base not read): the plan counts +1, the rule's minimum.

CraftSearch.SolverRaphaelTip:
Raphael, the solver also used by other crafting tools: it looks for the best sequence, can take longer and use more memory, and uses all processors but two. Its native library runs in the game's process: if it fails, the game can close. It also serves the crafting log panel, which then computes for each recipe you select. Its sequence is replayed in Tensho's simulator before it is proposed; a sequence that does not hold is refused.
Default: off.

Discord.Title: Discord
Discord.Help: Posts Tensho alarms in a channel of your Discord server through a webhook (Discord › channel settings › Integrations › Webhooks › Copy webhook URL). Nothing is sent until the address is entered and sending is turned on, except the « Send a test » button, on your click. Only the alarm's message is sent, and the character's name only if you add it. Alarms written into the game's list ring in the game; they are still posted to Discord. Clearing the address or turning sending off drops the messages still waiting.
Discord.EnabledTip:
When a Tensho alarm rings, its message is also posted in the webhook's channel below (network: Discord, over HTTPS). Turning it off drops the messages still waiting.
Default: off.
Discord.UrlTip: Address copied from Discord. It grants the right to post in the channel: do not share it. It is kept in the plugin's configuration on this PC, masked here, never written to the logs nor to the diagnostic report. Only Discord webhook addresses are accepted (discord.com, ptb.discord.com, canary.discord.com, discordapp.com). Saved when you leave the field; a new address drops the messages waiting for the old one.
Discord.ClearTip: Clears the webhook address: nothing is sent any more.
Discord.UrlInvalid: Address refused: it must be a Discord webhook address (https://discord.com/api/webhooks/…). It is not saved.
Discord.UsernameTip:
Name Discord shows for the messages (80 characters at most; a name containing « discord » or « clyde » is refused by Discord and replaced by « Tensho »).
Default: Tensho.
Discord.TemplateTip: Text posted for each alarm. Replaced markers: [label] the alarm's name, [minutes] the minutes before the time, [time] the local time, [character] the character's name (if allowed below). Empty: the default message. An alarm can have its own message (Alarms page, a group's slots).
Discord.CategoryTip:
Posts this category's alarms to Discord. Each alarm group can also be left out on the Alarms page.
Default: on.
Discord.CharacterTip:
Adds your character's name to the message (marker [character], else at the end). This is personal data: the whole channel sees it.
Default: off.
Discord.MentionTip: Numeric id of a Discord role (Discord developer mode › right-click the role › Copy ID), or its mention <@&…>: that role is mentioned at the start of each message. No other mention (@everyone, @here, players) is ever triggered. Empty: no mention.
Discord.TestTip: Posts a test message in the channel to check the address, one per click (tried again automatically only when Discord asks to wait or the connection could not be opened). The role set above is mentioned.
Discord.TestMessage: 🔔 Tensho Assistant test: alarms will arrive in this channel. Example: [label] in [minutes] min ([time]).
Discord.StatusRejected: Discord refused the message (code {0}): 401, 403 or 404 = check the webhook address; 400 = message refused.
Discord.StatusRateLimited: Discord is limiting posts (code {0}): message dropped, the next ones wait for the pause it asked for.
Discord.StatusNetwork: Discord unreachable or timed out: message not sent (or perhaps already posted when it timed out).
Discord.StatusInvalidAddress: Invalid webhook address: message not sent.
Discord.Counts: Sent: {0} · failed: {1} · dropped (queue full, address cleared or sending off): {2}
Discord.NeedsUrl: Sending is on but no valid address is saved.
Discord.GroupOnTip:
Posts this group's alarms to Discord when sending is on in the settings.
Default: on.
Discord.GroupMessageTip: Discord message of this group's alarms; same markers as the settings message ([label], [minutes], [time], [character]). Saved when you leave the field.

Credits.Title: Credits
Credits.Intro: Everything Tensho uses, taken from the code on 2 November 2026, with each licence read again at its source unless stated otherwise. Game data comes first; community data is used only when the game does not have it, always cited. A source with no published licence is never copied: a rule or formula from it is taken as a fact, with original code. Tensho is original code under the GPL v3 licence.
Credits.FilterTip: Filters the list by name, author, licence or use.

Kind.Reference: Plugins and sites read to understand

KindHelp.Game: Game data is read from your installation and is not shipped with Tensho, except the Mini Cactpot payout table, written into the code.
KindHelp.Library: Provided by Dalamud and .NET; Tensho does not embed them.
KindHelp.Embedded: Copied into Tensho with their source and the full licence notice in the file; refreshed by a new snapshot.
KindHelp.Online: Read on demand (page opened, hover, setting), over HTTPS, and kept in a disk cache (Discord only sends). A setting may turn only part of a source off: the source's row says so.
KindHelp.Rule: Community rules missing from the game data: taken as facts, original code, shown as estimates.
KindHelp.Reference: Read to understand the game or a behaviour; no code copied (AGPL or unlicensed ones included).
KindHelp.Tool: Used to build, check and publish Tensho; nothing ships in the plugin.

Copied.Embedded: Copied into Tensho: data, with the licence notice.
Copied.Rule: Taken as a fact: rule or formula, original code, no text copied.
Copied.Other: Taken into Tensho: data or table, source cited.

Credits.ReadOnly: Read or contacted only, nothing copied.

ToolDetails.Uses: Recipes, crafting leves, potential Grand Company deliveries, aquariums, orchestrion rolls and quest rewards. Variants and unknown states remain visible; daily requests and quest availability are not inferred.
ToolDetails.Fashion: This week: theme (game data) and each slot's category read in the game window, with the equipment reported by the community (FFXIVGachaSpreadsheet), owned pieces first, and reported dyes; optional buttons on the game window. Every category: choose a hint manually, filter by native slot, select items. Source dates are shown; no score is calculated.
ToolDetails.Gp: Compare a manual MIN/BTN scenario with already paid effects and a first-attempt bonus (Bountiful Yield II estimated from a community rule, editable). Optional node observation can copy GP, level and attempts. Starting values and effects remain manual; regeneration, restoration, procs, crystals and collectables are outside the model.
ToolDetails.Monsters: Monsters dropping the selected item: LuminaSupplemental first, then Console Games Wiki (cached copy) and, as a complement, Garland Tools on request (dated details, levels, locations, zone maps, selectable items). Coverage is partial; drop rates and live presence are not inferred.
ToolDetails.Duties: Manually fetch listed Garland Tools loot for a duty from the native catalog. Dated cache, chest categories and rewards remain separate. Items share the selected-item context. Coverage is partial; no drop rates are inferred.
ToolDetails.Triad: Card notebook (ordinary and Ex. cards, values, sort by side, sum or rule score), acquisitions, decks, manual advice with two known hands, NPCs to face, packs to buy and missing cards. Supports Reverse, Fallen Ace, Same/Plus and combos, Order, Ascension and Descension. Optional match observation, disabled by default: on your turn, advice framed on the game window; no move is played automatically.
ToolDetails.Macros: Sequences of personal and shared macros (32 at most). Each selected macro must end with /tenshonext (crafting macros written by Tensho with the « Chain the pages » option already have it). Start manually, stop at any time; this tool never changes saved macros. Validated in game with crafting macros (0.196).
ToolDetails.Maps: Tensho map (can replace the game map, M key) with game icons, quests and objectives, FATEs, sightseeing vistas, aether currents, coffers, NPC vendors, gathering points, player, party and edge markers; flag, teleport and a menu per icon. Map page: region and zone search, entered coordinates, saved bookmarks and zone resources.
ToolDetails.Cactpot: Exact solver for a manually entered ticket, with optional experimental observation of the in-game ticket. Advice updates after each revealed number; no automatic clicks.
ToolDetails.Character: Observed character attributes for combat, crafting and gathering; for combat jobs, computed real values (game level modifiers, community formulas), also beside the game's Character window (setting). Gear planning: Gear page.
ToolDetails.Blue: Native spellbook, confirmed learned spells, numbers, ranks, descriptions and listed locations. Missing sources and learning conditions remain incomplete.
ToolDetails.Quests: Native catalog, journal quest kinds and genres with their completion, confirmed progress, prerequisites, follow-up quests and variant rewards. Quests of the other starting cities and options not taken are hidden and left out of percentages (a checkbox shows them). Item uses link to quests offering that item. Links do not prove availability; other conditions, stages and resets still need verification.
ToolDetails.Market: NQ/HQ summary for the current world, Universalis listings for the world, data centre or region (filters, exact cost of N units, tax included) and sale history; dates and disk cache, last known value shown, dated, when Universalis fails. Compare direct ingredient costs and terminal chain requirements with manual batch lookup. Hover prices are optional in Settings and disabled by default.
ToolDetails.Collections: Mounts, minions, emotes, orchestrion, titles and achievements (cards are in the Triple Triad tool), with categories, details and linked rewards; hover a mount, minion, emote or song: how to obtain it; right-click: links to its sources. Titles and achievements are confirmed unacquired only when a complete stable list is received; otherwise their state remains unknown. No automatic unlocking or reward claims.
ToolDetails.Sorting: Profiles per character and storage, with reusable templates of matching geometry. Priority criteria, protected or filtered zones, bidirectional filling and previews preserving empty slots. Apply explicitly to bags or open storage after live reading. Loading a template does not start sorting. Item type metadata does not prove stack marketability or character equipment eligibility. Native behavior needs in-game validation.
ToolDetails.Gathering: Gathering and fishing sources, filters, maps, Eorzea/local schedules, zone weather and alarms. Fish: GatherBuddy first (bait and mooch chain, bite and hookset, ET window, weather and previous weather, Teamcraft bite times), Garland Tools as a complement. Native fishing log descriptions, restrictions and tomes do not prove catches or unlocks. Calculate windows from stated criteria; missing criteria and uncertain results stay visible. No catch is guaranteed. Gathering and fishing helpers beside the game windows, optional MIN/BTN observation.
ToolDetails.Craft: Recipes, preparation, simulation and search, saved sequences and macro export (manual copy or writing into the game's macros over a chosen range, chained with /tenshonext). The companion panel follows the selected crafting-log recipe, compares saved sequences and suggests a macro to copy. Synthesis observation compares the next action in ordinary conditions; it never executes an action. Special recipes and native adaptive rotations remain unfinished.
ToolDetails.Bank: The bank combines the inventory, armoury chest, glamour dresser and armoire (the last two known once opened in the game) with complete retainer and saddlebag imports. Click an item to share it with other tools. Snapshots must be imported again after transfers.

Reminders.BingoOddsHelp: Exact count: the stickers left land at random on the empty cells (every placement counted); after a shuffle, the 9 stickers are anywhere. Helps decide whether to shuffle (second chance).
Reminders.TreasureShowTip: Opens the Tensho map on the spot of the deciphered treasure map you hold and places the flag there.
Reminders.ChallengeLogHelp: Challenge log entries done this week, read from the game once the log was opened (the game loads it only then).
Reminders.DomanEnclaveHelp: Donations made this week to the Doman Enclave reconstruction, against the week's cap; read from the game after a visit to the enclave.
Reminders.BingoHelp: Khloe's journal: stickers placed and second chance points, read from the game; it expires at the time shown.
Reminders.HuntBillsHelp: Number of hunt bills (elite and daily) held, read from the game.
Reminders.VoyagesHelp: Free company submarines and airships, from the last read in the workshop.
Reminders.Title: Reminders
Reminders.Description: The game's calendar timers (supply missions, custom deliveries, Fashion Report, allied societies, leves, treasure maps, retainer ventures) and company voyages: resets, counters read from the game, « done » boxes and alarms.
Reminders.SupplyHelp: Grand Company supply and provisioning missions; renewed every day at 20:00 UTC.
Reminders.DeliveriesHelp: Custom delivery clients; allowances renewed every Tuesday at 08:00 UTC.
Reminders.FashionHelp: New theme every Tuesday at 08:00 UTC (Fashion Report tool).
Reminders.AlliedHelp: Allied society daily quest allowance; renewed every day at 15:00 UTC.
Reminders.LevesHelp: Leve allowances: +3 every 12 hours (time read from the game).
Reminders.TreasureHelp: A treasure map can be deciphered every 18 hours. The game gives Tensho no time for it: click « Map opened » when you decipher one.
Reminders.TreasureOpenedTip: Notes that you just deciphered a map: Tensho counts 18 hours until the next. This wait is shared by all your characters.
Reminders.VenturesHelp: Retainer ventures in progress; read after opening the retainer list at a summoning bell.
Reminders.VenturesUnknown: Open the retainer list at a summoning bell
Reminders.DoneTip: Tick when done; the box clears itself at the next reset. It is shared by all your characters.
Reminders.AlarmTip: Creates an alarm for « {0} » at the next time shown.
Reminders.Help: Grand Company squadron and Ehcatl deliveries come next (data to be read in game).
Reminders.SquadronMissionHelp: Grand Company squadron mission in progress and its end time, read from the game (no need to be at the barracks).
Reminders.SquadronTrainingHelp: Grand Company squadron training in progress and its end time, read from the game (no need to be at the barracks).

FreeCompany.Title: Free company
FreeCompany.Description: Submarines and airships read in the company workshop: rank, route, return and finds of the last voyage (Vessels), best submarine routes (Best routes), planned builds and route check (Builds).
FreeCompany.NoData: No vessel read yet. Enter the free company workshop (and open the voyage control panel if nothing shows): Tensho reads and keeps the submarines and airships.
FreeCompany.ReadAtTip: The game gives these values only in the company workshop; Tensho keeps the last read and updates it at each visit. With several companies, the most recent date is shown here; each company's date is in « Companies read », at the bottom of the tab.
FreeCompany.RouteUnknown: Route not given by the game
FreeCompany.LootHint: Click: finds of the last voyage (items and quantities).
FreeCompany.ReadUnavailable: The workshop could not be read in whole or in part (perhaps after a game update); what could not be read keeps its last read.
FreeCompany.ForgetTip: For a company you left: removes its vessels, unlocked sectors and build plans (Vessels, Best routes, Builds, Reminders). A second click confirms and saves it at once. A new visit to its workshop reads the vessels and sectors again, not the plans.

AirshipPlanner.VesselTip: Choosing an airship read in the workshop fills its rank, speed and range (still editable to try another build).
AirshipPlanner.SpeedTip: The airship's total speed: the game uses it to compute each leg and each survey.
AirshipPlanner.RangeTip: The airship's total range: the longest voyage, surveys included.
AirshipPlanner.GoalTip: Experience per day: takes the duration into account (back-to-back voyages). Experience per voyage: the most in one voyage. Shortest: the shortest duration. Loot value is unknown for airships: it ranks nothing.
AirshipPlanner.Computing: The game is computing the legs…
AirshipPlanner.NotLoggedIn: Log in with a character: the game computes the legs.
AirshipPlanner.Unavailable: Leg computation unavailable in this game version (functions not found or failing); details are in the Dalamud log.
AirshipPlanner.Unconfirmed: Durations and distances not confirmed in game.
AirshipPlanner.UnconfirmedTip: Each leg and each survey is computed by the game itself. How a voyage adds them up is not checked yet: legs from the start, surveys, a fixed 12 h, no return leg, times in seconds. Compare with the workshop's flight panel; report any gap on the repository.
AirshipPlanner.ChooseHint: Tick up to 5 sectors in the table to measure a route.
AirshipPlanner.ChooseTip: Adds this sector to the measured route (5 at most); the shortest visiting order is chosen.
AirshipPlanner.OverRange: Beyond the range: this route cannot depart.
AirshipPlanner.LegUnknown: The game gave no leg for this route: distance and duration unknown.
AirshipPlanner.Raw: Raw (developer mode): speed {0}, start → sector 1: {1} (time / distance), sector 1 survey: {2}
AirshipPlanner.UseTip: Replaces the ticked sectors with this route's.
AirshipPlanner.ClearTip: Unticks every sector of the measured route.
AirshipPlanner.ExpUnknownTip: At least one sector of this route has no experience in the game data (0): the experience shown is a minimum.
AirshipPlanner.ExpUnknownNote: Routes through a sector without known experience are only ranked by « Shortest ».

AirshipSectors.Unavailable: Airship sector data unavailable (perhaps after a game update); details are in the Dalamud log.
AirshipSectors.Help: The Sea of Clouds sectors: rank required, ceruleum tanks, base survey time, experience, and what unlocks them. The possible loot is a list of items without quantity or rate: the value of an airship voyage stays unknown.
AirshipSectors.FilterTip: Filters on the sector's name or on an item of its possible loot.
AirshipSectors.RankTip:
Shows only the sectors open at this rank (0 = all). Required rank read from the game data.
Default: 0.
AirshipSectors.UnlockTip: Sector whose voyage discovers this one, with the surveillance it asks (LuminaSupplemental data). Path from the start: {0}.
AirshipSectors.SurveyTip: Base survey time from the game data; the real time depends on the airship's speed.
AirshipSectors.Source: Sectors: game data. Unlocks and possible loot: LuminaSupplemental (Critical-Impact, GPL-3.0), embedded with their licence notice.

RoutePlanner.UsePlanTip: Takes the rank, speed and range of this submarine's planned build (Builds tab).
RoutePlanner.UnlockedOnlyTip:
Offers only the sectors read as unlocked in the company workshop.
Default: on.
RoutePlanner.UnlockedUnknown: Unlocked sectors not read yet: visit the workshop.
RoutePlanner.ToBuildTip: Opens this route in the Builds tab: distance, duration, breakpoints and best builds.
RoutePlanner.Help: Best submarine routes for a rank, speed and range: average loot value (community records × NPC sell price), computed time and distance. Hover a route to see the expected loot. Airships have no public loot records. Unlocked sectors are read in the chosen submarine's company workshop (« Unlocked sectors only » filter); before the first workshop visit, check in game that they are unlocked. « Planned build » takes the rank, speed and range of the build planned in the Builds tab; « Build » opens a route in that tab (breakpoints, duration, best builds). The price can also take your world's market into account (Universalis, « Market prices » button), and the loot can come from the records of one surveillance tier only.
RoutePlanner.VesselTip: Choosing a submarine read in the workshop fills its rank, speed and range (editable to try another build).
RoutePlanner.RankTip: Submarine rank: only sectors of this rank or lower are offered.
RoutePlanner.SpeedTip: Total speed (parts + rank bonus): shortens travel and surveys.
RoutePlanner.RangeTip: Total range (parts + rank bonus): maximum distance of a voyage, surveys included.
RoutePlanner.GoalTip: Value per voyage: the most rewarding loot of one voyage. Value per day: accounts for the duration (back-to-back voyages). Experience: base experience per day.
RoutePlanner.None: No route possible with these values.
RoutePlanner.Source: Loot: averages from {0}, extracted on {1}. Value: NPC sell price (game data).
RoutePlanner.NoLoot: Some sectors have no loot records.
RoutePlanner.MapTip: Exploration area whose sectors are combined into routes; choosing a submarine sets it to the area of its read route.
RoutePlanner.Unavailable: Submarine sector data unavailable (perhaps after a game update); details are in the Dalamud log.
RoutePlanner.UnlockedChoose: Several companies read: choose a submarine to filter the unlocked sectors.
RoutePlanner.PriceTip:
NPC sale: sell price from the game data.
NPC or market: for each item sold on the market board, your world's lowest NQ price (Universalis) when known and higher than the NPC price; otherwise the NPC price. Market prices are fetched with the « Market prices » button.
Default: NPC sale.
RoutePlanner.BandTip:
Records used for the average loot, by the surveillance of the submarines that made them (the source splits them so): all, below tier 2, at tier 2 or at tier 3. Your submarine's tier on each sector is shown in the Builds tab. A sector without a record at that tier keeps the average of all its records (shown on hover).
Default: all records.
RoutePlanner.FetchPricesTip: Fetches from Universalis your world's lowest NQ price for the listed routes' loot items whose price is missing, the most frequent first, 32 at most per click. The ranking is then redone.
RoutePlanner.FetchPricesNoWorld: World or character not known yet: log in with a character.
RoutePlanner.SourceMarket: Loot: averages from {0}, extracted on {1}. Value: the highest of the NPC sale and the lowest NQ price on {2} (Universalis); « ≥ »: some market prices are missing and count at the NPC price.
RoutePlanner.LootLineNoPrice: {0}: {1} on average, ~{2} gil (NPC {3} each, market price unknown)
RoutePlanner.BandFallback: A sector has no record at this surveillance tier: the average of all its records is used.
RoutePlanner.PricesMissing: {0} items sold on the market have no price: counted at the NPC price.
RoutePlanner.LootLineNoListing: {0}: {1} on average, ~{2} gil (NPC {3} each, no NQ listing on the market)

CharactersUi.Help: Every character Tensho has seen on this PC, one file each: bags, crystals, currencies and armoury recorded at each login, retainers and saddlebags when you opened them. « See » opens the Bank tab on that character.
CharactersUi.None: No character recorded yet: log in once with each.
CharactersUi.SeeTip: Opens the Bank tab on this character's storages.
CharactersUi.EraseTip: Erases everything Tensho recorded for this character (its file is deleted). A second click confirms.
CharactersUi.EraseCurrentTip: Erases everything Tensho recorded for the logged-in character; its bags, crystals, currencies and armoury will be recorded again within a few minutes. A second click confirms.
CharactersUi.Privacy: Characters are identified by the local id the game gives the logged-in character, never by the account id; nothing leaves this PC.

Undercut.Copied: {0}{3}: lowest offer {1}, price copied {2} (paste it with Ctrl+V)

ItemNotes.Help: Your note and labels on this item, kept on this PC. They show in the item information (hover and sheet). When you open an NPC shop, the chat lists your bags' items « to sell to an NPC » and « important ».
ItemNotes.TextTip: Free text (500 characters at most), saved when you leave the field.
ItemNotes.ImportantTip: Not to sell nor discard: a warning shows in the chat when you open an NPC shop with this item in your bags.
ItemNotes.ToSellTip: Reminder in the chat when you open an NPC shop with this item in your bags. Nothing is sold for you.
ItemNotes.ShopReminderTip:
When an NPC shop opens, lists in the chat your bags' items labelled « to sell » and « important ».
Default: on.
ItemNotes.ImportantSoundTip:
Plays the alarm sound when a shop opens with an « important » item in your bags.
Default: off.
ItemNotes.Count: {0} items noted out of {1} at most.
ItemNotes.Full: Too many items noted: remove notes before adding more.
ItemNotes.ShopToSell: To sell to an NPC in your bags: {0}
ItemNotes.ShopImportant: Careful, important items in your bags: {0}

StorageReport.Help: What could free space, without moving anything: stacks of one item that could be merged (your bags live, your saved saddlebags and retainers), armoury pieces no gear set uses, and items that can go to the armoire.
StorageReport.Merge: Stacks to merge ({0} slots to free)
StorageReport.MergeLine: {0}{1} — {2}: {3} stacks, {4} in all, {5} slots to free
StorageReport.Outside: Armoury: pieces outside every gear set ({0})
StorageReport.OutsideHelp: {0} gear sets read from the game; armoury recorded on {1}. A piece may serve as glamour or another use: check before selling it.
StorageReport.OutsideNone: Every armoury piece is used by a set.
StorageReport.SetsUnavailable: Gear sets unreadable in this game version; details are in the Dalamud log.
StorageReport.NoArmoury: Armoury not recorded yet: it is a few seconds after login.
StorageReport.ArmoireHelp: Items the armoire takes, kept elsewhere (bags, armoury outside gear sets, saddlebags, retainers, glamour dresser). Armoire saved on {0}.
StorageReport.ArmoireNotRead: Armoire not saved yet: open it once in game to know which are already there. Without the gear sets, the armoury is left out.
StorageReport.ArmoireNone: Nothing to put in the armoire.
StorageReport.ArmoireSpare: already in the armoire: this copy is spare
StorageReport.SameLookHelp: Dresser items with the same model and slot: one is often enough for glamour. Dresser saved on {0}. Check the dyes before discarding.
StorageReport.NoDresser: Glamour dresser not saved yet: open it once in game.
StorageReport.SameLookNone: No identical looks in the dresser.
StorageReport.Nothing: Report only: nothing is moved or sold for you.

ExternalLinks.Tip: Opens the item's page in your browser. The wiki is in English; the Lodestone follows Tensho's language.
ExternalLinks.Usage: Write an item name: /tensho wiki <item> or /tensho lodestone <item>.
ExternalLinks.Loading: Item catalogue loading; try again in a moment.
ExternalLinks.NoEnglish: English name unknown for this item: no wiki page.

GilJournal.Help: Every change of your gil, kept 90 days on this PC: the character's, your retainers' (known once the bell is opened) and the company chest's (while it is open). The category comes from the game window open when it changed (shop, market, repair, teleport…).
GilJournal.Unreadable: The saved journal could not be read: it is not written over (see the Dalamud log).
GilJournal.BalancesTip: Balances read from the game; « unknown » until the game gives them (retainer bell, open chest).

ShopRequirement.Tip: Condition for the shop to offer this article (game data). « Done » comes from your quest journal or your achievements read by Tensho.

ItemFilters.Title: Filters
ItemFilters.CategoryTip: Keeps only the items of this category (the one of the game's item window).
ItemFilters.EquipLevelTip: Level needed to wear the item, from … to … (0 = no limit).
ItemFilters.ItemLevelTip: Item level, from … to … (0 = no limit).
ItemFilters.SlotTip: Keeps only the gear worn in this slot.
ItemFilters.TradableTip: Keeps only items that can be traded.
ItemFilters.MarketableTip: Keeps only items sold on the market board.
ItemFilters.KeyItemsTip: Searches the key items (quest items, which do not go in the bags); they have no item sheet.

CurrencyValue.OpenTip: Shows what this currency buys at vendors, and what each unit is worth on the market.
CurrencyValue.Title: What to do with « {0} »?
CurrencyValue.Help: What the currency buys (vendor directory), its price in that currency, the lowest market price on your world (Universalis, recent) and the gil each unit of currency is worth when reselling, most profitable first. Mounts and minions are marked « owned » or « missing ».
CurrencyValue.FetchTip: Fetches from Universalis the missing prices of the items sold on the market, 32 at most per click.
CurrencyValue.None: The known vendors do not take this currency, or it is encoded and not resolved yet.

DutyProgress.FilterTip: Filters by the status read from the game for the logged-in character. A duty whose status is unknown stays in the « not completed » lists.
DutyProgress.Unknown: · progress: log in to read it

Roulettes.Title: Daily duty roulettes
Roulettes.Unknown: Log in to read today's completed roulettes.
Roulettes.Help: Read from the game. The role bonus is the one the Duty Finder holds: if the column stays empty, open the Duty Finder once.

CollectionSources.FilterTip: Shows only the entries whose unlocking item has this source, from the same data as the right-click menu. « No known source » does not mean « cannot be obtained ».

Wishlist.Title: Wishlist
Wishlist.Full: Wishlist full ({0} items): remove one first.
Wishlist.Help: Items you want to get: right-click any item in Tensho › « Add to my wishlist ». Right-click a row for its sources.
Wishlist.RowTip: Right click: the item's tools and sources.

VistaLog.MissingOnlyTip: Hides the vistas already discovered (read in game).
VistaLog.NowOnlyTip: Keeps only the vistas whose Eorzea time window is open and whose weather (wiki) is the zone's weather now. Unknown weather: kept, marked « time OK ».

Outfits.Title: Outfits
Outfits.Help: Glamour dresser outfits: the game makes an outfit once all its pieces are in the dresser. « Owned » counts your bags and this character's saved storages. Right-click a piece: its sources.
Outfits.FilterMissingTip: Outfits missing at least one piece.
Outfits.FilterReadyTip: Every piece owned, not stored as an outfit yet (those already in the dresser first).
Outfits.FilterStoredTip: Outfits already stored in the dresser.
Outfits.Count: {0} stored out of {1} · {2} ready to store (every piece in the dresser)

Leves.Title: Guildleves
Leves.Description: Game data · state read in game for the logged-in character
Leves.Unknown: Guildleve state not read: log in.
Leves.TypeTip: Leve type (battle, crafting, gathering, Grand Company…).
Leves.ClientTip: The client who gives the leve.
Leves.FilterNotCompletedTip: Leves never completed; an unknown state stays in this list.

HuntingLog.Title: Hunting log
HuntingLog.Description: Game data · kills read in game for the logged-in character
HuntingLog.LogTip: A class log, or your Grand Company's log (the other companies are not shown).
HuntingLog.RankTip: Log rank. The game keeps the kills of the current rank only: earlier ranks are done, later ones not started.
HuntingLog.MissingOnlyTip: Hides the entries whose monsters are all done.
HuntingLog.None: Nothing to show for these filters.

ExtraCollections.Loading: Reading from the game… (log in if nothing appears)

BlueSpellSources.IndexFailed: Wiki spellbook unavailable (next try in a minute).
BlueSpellSources.SpellOrderTip: Sorts every spell by the level of the monster that teaches it (the lower of world monster and duty), from the wiki's spellbook, read at once when the page opens. Spells with no monster (default, quest…) stay last.
BlueSpellSources.IndexOff: Wiki off: level order limited to the copies already read.
BlueSpellSources.OrderTip: Order of the monsters: by level (a range « 43-48 » counts as 43; no level = last) or as on the wiki.
BlueSpellSources.Missing: The wiki has no « {0} » page: no information about this spell's monsters.
BlueSpellSources.Title: Monsters that teach it (wiki)
BlueSpellSources.Help: Click to read the spell's wiki page: only the English spell name is sent.
BlueSpellSources.Empty: The wiki lists no monster for this spell (it may be learned another way, a quest for instance).

AchievementProgress.TrackTip: Adds this achievement to the « Tracked achievements » list, at the top of the Achievements tab.
AchievementProgress.AskTip: Asks the game for this achievement's progress (one request to the server, on this click only). It is also read when you open the achievement in the game's window.
AchievementProgress.Wait: Wait a few seconds before asking for progress again.

Titles.WearTip: Changes the title your character wears (game function).
Titles.ForJobTip: This title will be worn when you change to this job, if « Change title with the job » is on.
Titles.RandomTip: Wears an obtained title picked at random.
Titles.ByJobTip: When you change job, wears the title chosen for it (not at login). Off by default.
Titles.ByJobEmpty: No title chosen per job: open an obtained title and click « … title ».

OrchestrionPlayer.NoRoll: The music playing has no orchestrion roll.
OrchestrionPlayer.FavoriteTip: Adds this roll to your favourites, at the top of the Orchestrion tab.

AutoAlarms.SettingTip: Creates a Tensho alarm at the end of each retainer venture (known once the retainer list was opened) and at each vessel's return (known after the workshop). The time follows the readings; the alarm goes an hour after it rang. No game alarm is ever made automatically.

ChatLinks.Title: Chat map links ({0})
ChatLinks.Help: Map links seen in the chat since login (hunt trains, treasure maps, meeting points). Kept in memory only, never saved; cleared at logout. 100 at most.
ChatLinks.Off: Reading is off: Tensho map settings, « Chat map links ».
ChatLinks.ChannelTip: Channels shown in the list; « All channels » brings them all back.
ChatLinks.ClearTip: Clears the kept links (nothing is saved to disk).
ChatLinks.Empty: No map link seen in these channels.
ChatLinks.FlagTip: Places the game flag on this point, like the page's « Open » button.
ChatLinks.AetheryteTip: Opens the Tensho map on this point and offers the nearest aetheryte of this map from your teleport list, with its cost. You teleport only if you confirm.
ChatLinks.NoAttuned: No aetheryte of this map is in your teleport list.

CharacterStatus.Title: Your characters ({0})
CharacterStatus.Help: What Tensho read for each of your characters at its last login: retainer ventures (after opening the retainer list), next treasure map, Wondrous Tails, hunt bills, today's roulettes. One file per character, local character id only. The « done » boxes above belong to the logged-in character.
CharacterStatus.Empty: No character read yet: log in, the row appears within 30 seconds.
CharacterStatus.EraseTip: Erases this character from Tensho and deletes its file (not possible for the logged-in character).

Squadron.Title: Squadron missions
Squadron.Help: Reads your squadron in the barracks and ranks the parties of four for a mission, from the game's data. The success percent is an estimate (sheet rule, not yet checked in game); chemistry is not counted.
Squadron.ReadTip: Reads the members and the training bonus from the game. The game holds them only while you are in your Grand Company barracks (open the squadron there first).
Squadron.NotLoaded: The squadron is not loaded: go to your Grand Company barracks, open the squadron, then read again.
Squadron.Unavailable: The squadron could not be read (perhaps after a game update); details are in the Dalamud log.
Squadron.SheetsUnavailable: The squadron data of the game could not be read; details are in the Dalamud log.
Squadron.PickMissionTip: The squadron missions of the game; the mission running is chosen first.
Squadron.SetTip: The game shows one of these six requirement sets for this mission: choose the one in its window (physical / mental / tactical).
Squadron.NoParty: No party of four free members with known attributes.
Squadron.Estimate: Estimate: base percent of the mission plus each attribute reached (game data); not yet checked against the game, chemistry not counted.
Squadron.LogTip: Writes the squadron as read, the attributes used and these parties to the Dalamud log, to compare with the game window.
Squadron.Logged: Squadron written to the Dalamud log.

Garden.PageDescription: Your beds and pots with their reminders, and the crossbreeds of seeds with a planting plan. Plantings are noted automatically from the game's chat lines (setting below).
Garden.Title: Garden journal ({0})
Garden.Help: Note your garden beds and pots. Pick the seed to fill its growing and tending hours (community data, Lotlab), or type them. Tensho shows when each is ripe and when to tend it.
Garden.AlertsTip:
A chat line (and the alarms' sound if they play one) when a bed is ripe or needs tending, once each.
Default: on.
Garden.DetectTip:
Tensho reads the game's chat lines: when the game says you planted seeds, the bed is added to the journal with its seed (read in the planting window), its time and its hours. Tending and harvesting are not detected yet: the buttons stay. Nothing is sent or done in the game.
Default: on.
Garden.DetectedUnknown: Garden: a planting was seen in the chat, but not its seed: add it to the journal by hand.
Garden.TendTip: You tended it now: the next tending is counted from now. Greyed without a tending interval.
Garden.RemoveTip: Removes this bed from the journal at once.
Garden.PlaceTip: Where the bed or pot is, in your own words (1 to 40 characters).
Garden.SeedTip: What you planted, in your own words (1 to 40 characters).
Garden.SeedSearchTip: Shows only the seeds whose name contains this text.
Garden.CrossesHelp: Two seeds planted side by side can give a third. Community pairs (FFXIV Crossbreed Helper), shown with the game's item names.
Garden.CrossesUnavailable: The crossbreeding pairs could not be read; details are in the Dalamud log.
Garden.CrossesGivesTip: Lists the pairs of seeds that can give the chosen seed.
Garden.PairsHelp: The pairs that can give the fewest other seeds come first: the fewer the others, the more of this seed you get. Click a pair for its planting plan.
Garden.PlanOrder: Plant in the order of the numbers, alternating the two seeds: 4 of each, on a Deluxe Garden Patch (8 beds). A seed crosses when it is planted, next to a seed already there: bed 1 has no neighbour, so it gives no crossbreed; replant it once the others are in.
Garden.PlanSoil: Soil: {0} (about 90 %), or {1} (about 50 %). Fertilizing and watering do not change it.
Garden.PlanSource: Rules from the Console Games Wiki, not checked by Tensho; other patches are not covered.
Garden.CrossesUsesTip: Lists what the chosen seed can give, and the seed to plant next to it.
Garden.CrossesPickTip: The seeds named by the crossbreeding pairs, in the game's language.
Garden.CrossesSource: {0} pairs from FFXIV Crossbreed Helper (nick75g, MIT). Flowerpot flowers, including the Dawntrail ones, do not crossbreed.
Garden.CrossesUnmatched: {0} source names not found in the game's items (left out).
Garden.SeedPickTip: Fills the seed, its growing hours and its tending hours (when it starts to wilt without care) from the community data of Lotlab's Gardening Tracker. You can change them before planting.
Garden.SeedPickNone: The seed list could not be read; type the seed and the hours.
Garden.GrowTip: Hours until it is ripe (1 to 720): filled from the seed list, or typed.
Garden.TendHoursTip: Hours between two tendings (0 = no tending reminder, at most 168).
Garden.Invalid: Type a place and a seed (1 to 40 characters each).

PersonalTasks.Title: Your tasks ({0})
PersonalTasks.Help: Your own tasks: each day or each week (the game's resets), every n hours after doing them, or a counter up to a target (reset by hand). 50 at most.
PersonalTasks.PanelTip: Shows on screen, outside the Tensho window, the tasks marked « On screen » that are not done. Hidden in combat. Closing it turns this setting off.
PersonalTasks.DoneTip: Marks the task done; it comes back at its next reset.
PersonalTasks.OnScreenTip: Shows this task in the « to do » panel while it is not done.
PersonalTasks.ResetCounterTip: Sets the counter back to zero.
PersonalTasks.HoursTip: The task comes back this many hours after it was done (1 to 168).
PersonalTasks.AddTip: Adds the task to the list.
PersonalTasks.InvalidName: Give a name of 1 to 60 characters.

GearWear.Title: Wear and spiritbond
GearWear.Help: Condition and spiritbond of the worn pieces, read from the game every second. Condition is the game's percentage; spiritbond is read in points (10,000 = 100 %, to confirm in game).
GearWear.AlertTip: A chat message (and the alarm sound) when a worn piece goes below the repair threshold or reaches the spiritbond threshold. Once per crossing; the alarm options (silence in duties) apply.
GearWear.BarTip: A small on-screen bar with the lowest condition and the highest spiritbond of the worn pieces; drag it with the mouse.
GearWear.RepairBelowTip: Condition threshold (%) below which a piece needs repair. Default: 10 %.
GearWear.SpiritbondAtTip: Spiritbond threshold (%) from which materia can be extracted. Default: 100 %.
GearWear.BarConditionTip: Lowest condition of the worn pieces.
GearWear.BarSpiritbondTip: Highest spiritbond of the worn pieces.
GearWear.AlertExtract: {0} worn piece(s) ready for materia extraction.

Gear.MateriaKindTip: Stat of this socket's materia, at the highest grade allowed here; « — » removes it. In warning colour, it would go over the piece's cap.
Gear.MateriaGradeTip: Materia grade; when overmelding, only allowed grades are offered. In warning colour, it would go over the piece's cap.
Gear.ImportUnknown: No piece of this code is known to your client or fits its slot (code from a newer patch?): your plans are unchanged.
Gear.MateriaClearTip: Removes every planned materia of this slot: the piece counts with no materia, a worn piece included (its own no longer count in the plan).
Gear.WornUnavailable: The worn gear cannot be read (perhaps after a game update): the planner resumes at the next successful read (tried every 30 seconds). Your plans are kept.
Gear.OvermeldRateTip: Chance that melding succeeds in this overmeld slot: it depends on the grade, the slot's rank and the piece's quality (NQ or HQ). Grades I to X: read from the game data. Grades XI and XII: the game data has none; the rate comes from FFXIV Teamcraft (« per Teamcraft »), whose rates I to X are the same as the game's. A failure consumes the materia.

VesselBuilds.RouteRankTooLow: This route needs rank {0} (plan: rank {1}): the game will not accept it, no build is offered.
VesselBuilds.VesselTip: A submarine or airship read in the workshop (its read build is the starting point), or manual input. One plan is kept per vessel.
VesselBuilds.RankTip: Planned rank: it sets the capacity, the rank bonus (submarines) and the parts allowed.
VesselBuilds.UseReadTip: Forgets this vessel's plan: the build read in the workshop is the reference again.
VesselBuilds.PartsUnknown: Parts not read yet: visit the workshop (read since 0.315).
VesselBuilds.AirshipNote: Airships: stats, capacity and part ranks (game data). No loot breakpoints and no route planner: no public data under a compatible licence.
VesselBuilds.Sources: Parts, ranks and capacity: game data. Breakpoints: SubmarineTracker (MIT, from Elena's community sheet). Wear: community estimate. « cost ≤ capacity » rule: community tools.
VesselBuilds.CostTip: Sum of the parts' component points, against the rank's capacity (community tools' rule, not verified in game below rank 50).
VesselBuilds.PartRankTip: Rank required by the most advanced part; it must not exceed the vessel's rank.
VesselBuilds.RepairTip: Repair materials needed for the four parts (sum of the sheet values).
VesselBuilds.IdentifierTip: Short name used by the community: one letter per part (hull, stern, bow, bridge) — S Shark, U Unkiu, W Whale, C Coelacanth, Y Syldra; « + » for a modified part, « ++ » when all four are.
VesselBuilds.Mismatch: ⚠ The read stats do not match the computation (parts + rank bonus).
VesselBuilds.MismatchTip: Read in the workshop: {0}. Computed: {1}. Please report it: the computation is not verified in game yet.
VesselBuilds.CurrentRouteTip: Takes this submarine's current route (read in the workshop).
VesselBuilds.NoRoute: No route: use a route's « Build » button in Best routes, or « Current route ».
VesselBuilds.BreakpointsUnknown: Breakpoints unknown for at least one sector of this route.
VesselBuilds.SurveillanceTip: Surveillance: from tier 2 or 3, a chance at that tier's loot (community breakpoints).
VesselBuilds.RetrievalTip: Retrieval: sets the quantity (poor, normal, optimal; community breakpoints).
VesselBuilds.FavorTip: Favor: at the breakpoint, a chance at a second item per sector (community breakpoint).
VesselBuilds.Wear: Estimated wear: about {0} voyages before repair ({1} points per voyage out of 30,000).
VesselBuilds.WearTip: Community estimate: per sector, (335 + sector rank - part rank) × 7; the most worn part counts.
VesselBuilds.WantSurveillanceTip: Surveillance tier wanted over the whole route.
VesselBuilds.WantRetrievalTip: Retrieval tier wanted over the whole route.
VesselBuilds.WantFavorTip: Require the favor breakpoint (double item) over the whole route.
VesselBuilds.NoBuild: No build of this rank reaches these tiers with the range needed.
VesselBuilds.Unavailable: Vessel part data unavailable (perhaps after a game update); details are in the Dalamud log.
VesselBuilds.ApplyTip: Replaces and saves this vessel's plan with this build at once (the current plan is lost).
VesselBuilds.Unconfirmed: Tier not confirmed by records on this route.
VesselBuilds.UnconfirmedTip: On at least one sector of this route, the community breakpoint (SubmarineTracker) is lower than every FFXIVGachaSpreadsheet observation: a tier shown as reached may not be. Sectors: 81, 86, 92, 98, 105, 109, 111, 112, 121, 125, 126, 130, 132, 133, 144 to 148.
